## 3.1 Our Community Vision

Fourth Idly is built to make meaningful donations easier to give, receive, collect, transport, and deliver. The Platform brings together Donors, NGOs, Volunteers, and authorised Administrators around a common social-impact purpose.

These Community Guidelines establish the behavioural standards expected of everyone participating in the Fourth Idly community. They apply to activity within the mobile application and related Platform features, including Need Requests, Donations, Volunteer tasks, delivery coordination, chat, ratings, feedback, impact posts, and payment-related communications.

The Guidelines are intended to complement the Fourth Idly Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, and Data Deletion Policy. They are not exhaustive. Users are expected to act honestly, responsibly, safely, and respectfully even where a particular situation is not expressly listed.
## 3.2 Respectful Conduct
Every person using Fourth Idly deserves to be treated with dignity and respect. Users must communicate in a manner appropriate to a community built around charitable giving and service.
• Communicate courteously and professionally with Donors, NGOs, Volunteers, beneficiaries, and Platform staff.
• Treat disagreements and misunderstandings calmly and constructively.
• Respect cultural, linguistic, regional, socioeconomic, and other differences among people using the Platform.
• Do not demean, humiliate, threaten, intimidate, or deliberately embarrass another person.
• Do not use language, images, or behaviour that reduces beneficiaries or communities to stereotypes or their circumstances.
• Respect reasonable boundaries when communicating through chat, calls, pickup arrangements, or other delivery coordination.
Fourth Idly does not tolerate behaviour that undermines the dignity, safety, or trust of the people participating in the donation process.
## 3.3 Ethical Donations

Donors are responsible for ensuring that goods offered through the Platform are appropriate for donation and suitable for the stated Need Request. The Platform is intended to help useful items reach genuine needs, not to provide a channel for disposing of unsafe or prohibited materials.
• Donate only goods that are lawful, safe, usable, and reasonably suitable for the intended recipient.
• Describe the type and quantity of the item accurately.
• Be transparent about material limitations, condition, packaging, or other characteristics that may affect usability.
• Food should be handled hygienically and should not knowingly be expired, spoiled, contaminated, or unsafe.
• Do not offer hazardous, counterfeit, stolen, illegal, or otherwise prohibited goods.
• Do not deliberately substitute materially different goods from those represented to the NGO.
• Do not donate an item that you know is unsafe simply because you no longer want it.
• Complete agreed pickup or handover arrangements responsibly once a donation has been accepted.

Fourth Idly does not take ownership of donated goods merely because a Donation is created through the Platform. Users should exercise appropriate care and judgement regarding the safety and suitability of items.
## 3.4 Honest Need Requests
NGOs using Fourth Idly have a responsibility to ensure that Need Requests reflect genuine requirements. Trust in the Platform depends on Donors being able to understand what is actually needed.
• Create Need Requests only for genuine organisational or beneficiary needs.
• Accurately describe whether the request concerns Food or Products.
• Provide accurate quantities and units.
• Give a clear and truthful description of the requested item.
• Set a realistic required-by date and time.
• Do not exaggerate urgency to attract additional donations.
• Do not create duplicate or misleading requests for the same need.
• Update or close requests when the required quantity has been fulfilled or the need no longer exists.
• Provide accurate pickup information when a pickup location is supplied.
• Use donated goods for the charitable or social-impact purpose represented by the Need Request.
The current Platform automatically treats open listings as expired after their live-until date/time and may notify the NGO of expiry. Users should nevertheless maintain accurate and current requests.
## 3.5 NGO Accountability and Verification

NGO accounts are subject to an administrative verification process in the current Fourth Idly flow. An NGO may be required to provide a licence or registration ID and supporting licence/registration PDF before its account becomes active.
• Provide authentic and valid registration/licence information.
• Do not upload forged, altered, misleading, or unauthorised documents.
• Ensure that information submitted during verification belongs to the relevant organisation.
• Maintain accurate organisational profile and contact information.
• Notify Fourth Idly where material information changes and the Platform provides a mechanism to update it.
• Respond reasonably to Platform enquiries concerning a Need Request, donation, complaint, or verification issue.
• Confirm receipt of delivered donations accurately.
• Rate other participants honestly and in good faith.
• Use impact-post features truthfully and responsibly.

Verification indicates that Fourth Idly has reviewed the submitted information for Platform purposes. It should not be represented as a guarantee, endorsement, certification, or financial assessment of the NGO.
## 3.6 No Fraud or Misrepresentation
Fraud, deception, and deliberate misrepresentation are strictly prohibited. Examples include:
• Creating a fake NGO, Donor, or Volunteer identity.
• Submitting forged or fraudulent NGO licence/registration documents.
• Submitting a fraudulent Volunteer driving licence or other verification information.
• Impersonating another person, organisation, government authority, or Platform representative.
• Creating duplicate accounts to evade a restriction, suspension, or ban.
• Creating false Need Requests to obtain goods without a genuine charitable purpose.
• Misrepresenting the quantity, nature, condition, or destination of donated goods.
• Misappropriating donated goods for personal gain.
• Manipulating donation, delivery, rating, or payment workflows.
• Falsely claiming that a payment was made or received.
• Providing a false payment reference ID or using payment information to mislead another User.
• Using fabricated ratings, reviews, accounts, bots, or other artificial methods to manipulate Platform reputation or visibility.
Suspected fraud may result in immediate restriction, administrative investigation, account suspension or blocking, and, where appropriate or legally required, referral to relevant authorities.
## 3.7 Payment Integrity
The current Fourth Idly delivery flow may involve a Delivery Fee paid by a Donor to a Volunteer through UPI. Because the payment process affects trust between participants, Users must act honestly.
• Use the UPI details presented through the Platform only for the relevant delivery transaction.
• Do not alter or misrepresent the amount of the applicable Delivery Fee.
• Do not falsely claim that a payment has been completed.
• Do not falsely claim that a received payment was not received.
• Do not pressure another User to disclose a UPI PIN, OTP, banking password, or other confidential banking credential.
• Do not request banking credentials through Platform chat.
• Where a payment dispute occurs, provide truthful information and any available reference information.
• Do not manipulate or repeatedly submit verification actions to create a false payment state.
The Platform may route a payment dispute to an Admin for review. Users should cooperate honestly with reasonable verification requests.
## 3.8 Safe Communication
Fourth Idly provides communication features, including chat associated with donation and volunteer workflows. Users should use these channels responsibly and protect their own privacy.
• Do not share passwords, OTPs, UPI PINs, banking passwords, or other authentication secrets through chat.
• Do not request another User’s Aadhaar number, full banking credentials, or unnecessary sensitive information.
• Do not send spam, bulk messages, or repeated unwanted communications.
• Do not use chat to solicit unrelated commercial services or personal financial gain.
• Do not threaten, blackmail, intimidate, or harass another User.
• Do not knowingly send malicious files, links, code, or other harmful material.
• Be cautious of requests to move a transaction outside the Platform where doing so could create a safety, fraud, or payment risk.
• Report suspicious or unsafe communications through the available Platform or support channels.
Platform staff will not require Users to disclose passwords or confidential authentication credentials through ordinary support communications.
## 3.9 No Harassment
Harassment is prohibited whether it occurs through chat, donation coordination, pickup/delivery interactions, ratings, comments, impact posts, or other Platform activity.
• Do not send repeated unwanted messages after a person has indicated that communication is unwelcome.
• Do not make threats or implied threats.
• Do not target another User with repeated malicious reports or complaints.
• Do not publish another person’s private information without appropriate authority or consent.
• Do not engage in sexual harassment or sexually inappropriate communications.
• Do not intimidate NGO staff, Volunteers, Donors, beneficiaries, or other community members.
• Do not use ratings or feedback as a tool for retaliation, coercion, or personal revenge.
Where harassment is reported, Fourth Idly may review relevant Platform records and take action proportionate to the circumstances.
## 3.10 No Hate Speech or Discrimination

Fourth Idly aims to maintain an inclusive environment. Users must not post or communicate content that attacks, dehumanises, or promotes hostility toward people or groups based on protected or otherwise personal characteristics.
• Hate speech or degrading statements targeting a person or group.
• Content that promotes discrimination, exclusion, or hostility.
• Dehumanising or threatening language.
• Discriminatory descriptions in Need Requests, profiles, ratings, chat, or impact posts.
• Symbols or imagery used to promote hateful or violent ideologies.
• Harassment disguised as jokes, insults, stereotypes, or repeated targeting.
Content that violates these standards may be removed, and accounts responsible for serious or repeated violations may be restricted or permanently blocked.
## 3.11 No Illegal or Dangerous Activities
The Platform must not be used to facilitate illegal, dangerous, or prohibited activity. Users must comply with applicable Indian law and any other law applicable to their conduct.
• Do not use Fourth Idly to traffic stolen, counterfeit, prohibited, or illegally obtained goods.
• Do not distribute controlled substances or regulated items through an unauthorised donation.
• Do not use the Platform for money laundering, financial fraud, or payment manipulation.
• Do not use the donation workflow to conceal unlawful transactions.
• Do not knowingly violate intellectual-property or privacy rights.
• Do not exploit children, vulnerable persons, beneficiaries, or other community members.
• Do not use the Platform for any activity that creates an unreasonable safety risk to Donors, NGOs, Volunteers, beneficiaries, or Platform personnel.

Where an activity is regulated or requires a licence, Users are responsible for ensuring that they have the necessary legal authority before offering, transporting, receiving, or distributing the relevant item.
## 3.12 Authentic Profiles and Information
Users must maintain truthful and reasonably current information. This is particularly important because the current application uses role-based access and administrative verification.
• Use your own account and do not impersonate another person.
• Do not create multiple accounts for the purpose of manipulating the Platform or evading restrictions.
• Do not share your account credentials with another person.
• Keep contact information reasonably current so that donation and delivery coordination can function.
• Provide genuine information during NGO or Volunteer verification.
• Do not manipulate ratings, review totals, task status, payment status, or other Platform records.
• Do not use bots, scripts, automation, purchased reviews, or other artificial methods to manipulate Platform activity.
## 3.13 Volunteer Behaviour
Volunteers play a direct role in the physical movement of donated goods. They are expected to act responsibly from acceptance through pickup and delivery.
• Accept a delivery task only when you reasonably intend and are able to perform it.
• Arrive at pickup locations in a timely and responsible manner.
• Follow the pickup → delivery workflow accurately.
• Treat Donors, NGO representatives, beneficiaries, and other people respectfully.
• Handle donated goods with reasonable care during transportation.
• Do not intentionally delay, divert, conceal, sell, or misuse donated goods.
• Do not misrepresent pickup or delivery status.
• Use only lawful and safe transportation practices.
• Do not request or disclose unnecessary personal information.
• Keep UPI information accurate where it is used for Delivery Fee payments.
• Respond truthfully to payment-verification prompts.
• Report safety concerns, suspicious behaviour, damaged goods, or serious delivery problems through the appropriate Platform channel.

Volunteer verification may require a driving licence ID and supporting driving licence PDF. Approval does not relieve a Volunteer of responsibility for complying with applicable traffic, transport, safety, and other laws.
## 3.14 Donor Behaviour
Donors should approach the Platform with the purpose of fulfilling genuine NGO needs rather than simply disposing of unwanted items.
• Review the Need Request before donating.
• Donate items that reasonably match the request.
• Provide accurate quantity and item information.
• Follow agreed pickup or handover arrangements.
• Treat NGO representatives and Volunteers respectfully.
• Do not pressure an NGO to accept an unsuitable item.
• Do not misuse ratings or feedback to punish a User for an honest disagreement.
• Pay any applicable Delivery Fee honestly through the supported UPI workflow.
• Do not falsely claim payment or attempt to avoid an applicable fee through deception.
## 3.15 NGO Standards After Delivery
When donated goods reach the NGO, the NGO should accurately confirm receipt through the Platform’s pending-receipt flow.
• Confirm delivery only when the relevant goods have actually been received.
• Do not falsely report non-receipt where goods were delivered.
• Report material discrepancies or delivery issues promptly.
• Rate Donors and Volunteers fairly and based on actual interaction.
• Use donated goods for the charitable purpose represented in the Need Request.
• Maintain appropriate internal records of donations and distribution where required by the organisation’s own obligations.
• Do not commercially resell donated goods contrary to the represented charitable purpose or applicable agreement.
## 3.16 Ratings and Feedback Integrity
Ratings are intended to help build trust within the Fourth Idly community. They must reflect genuine experiences.
• Submit ratings based on an actual donation, delivery, or other eligible interaction.
• Do not purchase, sell, trade, or solicit positive ratings.
• Do not threaten another User to obtain a favourable rating.
• Do not submit multiple ratings through duplicate or fraudulent accounts.
• Keep written feedback factual and relevant.
• Do not include private information that another person has not authorised you to publish.
• Do not use ratings to discriminate against or harass another User.

The current Platform may calculate average ratings and total review counts from eligible activity. Fourth Idly may review, restrict, or remove ratings that appear fraudulent, abusive, retaliatory, or otherwise inconsistent with these Guidelines.
## 3.17 Impact Posts and Community Content

Fourth Idly may encourage or provide a flow for NGOs and other eligible participants to create impact posts after completed donations. Such posts can help the community understand the social impact of donations, but they must be created responsibly.
• Post truthful information about the donation or impact described.
• Do not fabricate beneficiaries, quantities, outcomes, or events.
• Do not use impact posts to solicit unauthorised financial payments.
• Do not publish another person’s private information without appropriate permission.
• Obtain appropriate consent before publishing identifiable photographs or recordings of beneficiaries or other individuals where required.
• Do not exploit images of vulnerable people for sensationalism, humiliation, or personal promotion.
• Do not post content that violates intellectual-property, privacy, or other legal rights.
• Do not use impact content to attack, shame, or retaliate against another User.
## 3.18 Protection of Beneficiaries
Beneficiaries may be in vulnerable circumstances. Users must protect their dignity and privacy.
• Do not photograph or record beneficiaries without appropriate informed permission where required.
• Do not publish names, addresses, medical information, identity documents, or other sensitive personal information without lawful authority and appropriate consent.
• Do not use beneficiaries’ circumstances as a means of humiliation, entertainment, or personal gain.
• Do not pressure beneficiaries to appear in photographs, videos, posts, or promotional material.
• Do not disclose precise locations or other information that could reasonably create a safety or privacy risk.
## 3.19 Safe Pickup and Delivery Practices
The current Fourth Idly flow may involve physical pickup and delivery. Users must prioritise safety over completing a Platform task.
• Do not undertake a pickup or delivery that would require unlawful or unsafe conduct.
• Use reasonable precautions when meeting another User.
• Do not enter a private premises where doing so would be unsafe or unauthorised.
• Do not carry prohibited or dangerous goods through the Platform.
• Do not drive or operate a vehicle in a manner that violates applicable law or creates an unreasonable risk.
• Communicate significant delays or safety concerns promptly.
• Where an immediate safety threat exists, prioritise personal safety and contact appropriate emergency services rather than attempting to resolve the matter solely through the Platform.
## 3.20 Platform and Technical Abuse
Users must not interfere with the operation, security, or integrity of Fourth Idly.
• Do not attempt to bypass authentication or role-based access controls.
• Do not access another User’s account or private records without authorisation.
• Do not scrape, harvest, copy, or systematically collect User information without permission.
• Do not reverse engineer, exploit, or interfere with Platform services except where expressly permitted by law.
• Do not upload malware, viruses, malicious code, or harmful files.
• Do not overload, disrupt, or attack Platform infrastructure.
• Do not manipulate Firestore records, notifications, payment statuses, ratings, or other application data through unauthorised methods.
• Do not attempt to exploit notification routing, payment verification, or task-assignment logic.
## 3.21 Reporting Violations
Users are encouraged to report conduct that may violate these Guidelines. Reports should be made honestly and with enough information to help Fourth Idly understand the issue.
• Use any reporting or support functionality made available within the Platform.
• Provide the relevant donation, task, message, or User information where available.
• Explain what occurred and, where possible, when it occurred.
• Provide supporting screenshots or other evidence where appropriate and lawful.
• Do not knowingly submit false reports.
Where the current interface does not provide a dedicated reporting control for a particular issue, Users should use the official Fourth Idly support or grievance channel published by the Platform.
## 3.22 Handling of Reports

Fourth Idly may review reports using information available through Platform records, including relevant account information, donation records, task status, payment status, messages, ratings, notifications, and administrative records.

Where necessary, Fourth Idly may contact involved Users for clarification or additional information. Information relating to a report will be handled in accordance with the Privacy Policy and applicable law.
Fourth Idly cannot guarantee a particular outcome for every report. The Platform may take action where the available evidence indicates a violation, risk, abuse, or other concern.
## 3.23 Enforcement Actions
Violations of these Community Guidelines may result in action proportionate to the seriousness and circumstances of the conduct. Possible actions include:
• Informal guidance or warning.
• Removal, restriction, or modification of content that violates the Guidelines.
• Restriction of a Need Request, Donation, task, message, rating, or impact post.
• Temporary suspension of account access.
• Rejection or suspension of NGO or Volunteer verification.
• Blocking of an account.
• Permanent termination of access.
• Restriction of specific Platform features.
• Administrative review of a payment or delivery dispute.
• Referral to law-enforcement or other appropriate authorities where required or reasonably appropriate.
Fourth Idly may take immediate action where necessary to protect Users, beneficiaries, Platform security, or the integrity of a donation or payment workflow.
## 3.24 Appeals and Clarification
Where an account or content is restricted, the User may contact the official Fourth Idly support or grievance channel to request clarification or appeal where an appeal mechanism is available.

An appeal should explain why the User believes the action was incorrect and provide relevant information. Fourth Idly may consider additional evidence, the severity of the violation, previous conduct, and risks to the community when reviewing an appeal.
## 3.25 No Retaliation
Users must not retaliate against a person who makes a good-faith report, provides evidence during an investigation, declines an unsafe request, or participates in a Platform review.
• Do not threaten a reporting User.
• Do not manipulate ratings in retaliation.
• Do not send unwanted communications because someone reported or blocked you.
• Do not attempt to identify or expose a reporting person where confidentiality is required or reasonably expected.
• Do not create another account to continue targeting a User after restriction.
## 3.26 Cooperation with Administrative Reviews
Fourth Idly may conduct administrative reviews involving account verification, delivery issues, payment verification, payment disputes, complaints, suspicious activity, or ratings.

Users are expected to provide truthful information when reasonably requested. Deliberately providing false information, manipulating evidence, or obstructing an investigation may itself constitute a violation.
## 3.27 Third-Party and Off-Platform Conduct

Fourth Idly primarily governs conduct connected with Platform activity. However, conduct occurring outside the Platform may still be relevant where it directly affects a Fourth Idly donation, delivery, payment, safety matter, or another User’s ability to participate safely.

Users should be cautious when asked to move payments, exchange sensitive information, or otherwise bypass the Platform. Fourth Idly may be unable to protect Users or resolve disputes concerning arrangements made entirely outside its systems.
## 3.28 No Guarantee of User Conduct

These Guidelines establish standards but cannot guarantee that every User will comply with them. Fourth Idly may provide verification, notifications, ratings, administrative review, and reporting mechanisms to support trust, but Users remain responsible for exercising reasonable judgement and taking appropriate precautions.
NGO verification, Volunteer approval, ratings, or Platform participation should not be treated as an absolute guarantee of another User’s conduct, suitability, financial reliability, or safety.
## 3.29 Relationship with Other Policies
These Community Guidelines form part of the broader Fourth Idly policy framework and should be read together with the Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, and Data Deletion Policy.
• The Terms and Conditions govern access to and use of the Platform.
• The Privacy Policy explains how personal data is processed.
• The Data Deletion Policy explains account and personal-data deletion.
• These Community Guidelines establish expected standards of conduct and community participation.

If there is a conflict between these Guidelines and mandatory applicable law, the law will prevail. If there is a conflict between these Guidelines and another Fourth Idly policy, the relevant policy and circumstances will be interpreted consistently wherever reasonably possible.
## 3.30 Updates to These Guidelines

Fourth Idly may update these Community Guidelines as the Platform evolves, new features are introduced, or legal and safety requirements change. Material changes may be communicated through the Platform or other appropriate channels.
Users are expected to review the current Guidelines periodically and comply with the version applicable to their use of the Platform.
## 3.31 Contact and Reporting Details

For reporting violations, serious safety concerns, privacy issues, payment disputes, or other community concerns, Users should use the official support, privacy, or grievance contact details published by Fourth Idly through the Platform or its official communications.

The final Fourth Idly reporting, grievance, and support email addresses should be inserted here once the official legal/contact details are confirmed. The Charitey email addresses from the source document have intentionally not been carried over.
## 3.32 Our Shared Standard

Fourth Idly works only when people can trust one another. A Donor must be able to trust that a Need Request is genuine. An NGO must be able to trust that a donation is honestly represented. A Volunteer must be able to trust that a delivery task and payment status are accurately represented. Every participant must be able to communicate without fear of harassment or exploitation.

Our expectation is simple: use Fourth Idly with honesty, care, dignity, and responsibility. The goal is not merely to complete a transaction. It is to make the entire journey from need to donation to delivery safer, clearer, and more meaningful for everyone involved.

paragraphs:
4. Cookie Policy
Effective Date: 1 July 2025 | Last Updated: 1 July 2025
4.1 What Are Cookies?
Cookies are small text files placed on your device (computer, tablet, or smartphone) by websites you visit. They are widely used to make websites function correctly, to remember your preferences, and to provide information to site owners about how the site is being used. Cookies cannot execute programs or deliver viruses to your device. They are uniquely assigned to you and can only be read by the web server that issued them.
In addition to cookies, Charitey may use similar technologies including local storage, session storage, and web beacons, all of which function in broadly similar ways. References to 'cookies' in this policy encompass these technologies unless otherwise specified.
4.2 Essential Cookies
Essential cookies are strictly necessary for the Charitey Platform to function. Without them, core services such as logging in, navigating between pages, and submitting forms would not work. These cookies do not collect personal information and cannot be switched off without impairing Platform functionality. Examples include:
Session cookies that maintain your login state while you browse.
CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) tokens that protect your account from malicious requests.
Load balancing cookies that direct requests to the appropriate server.
Security cookies that flag suspicious activity.
No consent is required for essential cookies under applicable law, as they are strictly necessary for the service you have requested.
4.3 Functional Cookies
Functional cookies allow the Platform to remember choices you have made and provide enhanced, personalised features. They may be set by Charitey or by third-party providers whose services we have integrated. Examples include:
Language and regional preference settings.
Remembering your login details (if you select 'stay logged in').
Storing display preferences such as accessibility settings.
These cookies are generally set only with your consent, except where they are necessary to provide a feature you have specifically requested.
4.4 Analytics Cookies
Analytics cookies help us understand how visitors interact with the Platform by collecting and reporting information anonymously. We use this data to improve the Platform's design, content, and performance. Information collected may include:
Which pages are visited most frequently.
How long users spend on each page.
Where users come from (referral source).
Which device and browser users are using.
Whether users complete key actions (such as submitting a donation listing).
Analytics data is aggregated and does not personally identify individual users. We may use tools such as Google Analytics or equivalent privacy-compliant analytics platforms. Where such tools are used, they are configured to anonymise IP addresses and comply with applicable data protection law.
4.5 Marketing Cookies
Charitey does not currently use marketing or advertising cookies. In the future, if we introduce paid advertising, partnerships, or targeted outreach campaigns, we may deploy marketing cookies to measure the effectiveness of campaigns and to show relevant content. Any introduction of marketing cookies will:
Be preceded by an update to this Cookie Policy and appropriate notice to users.
Require your explicit prior consent through a clear consent mechanism.
Be subject to your right to withdraw consent at any time.
4.6 Cookie Consent
When you first visit the Platform, you will be presented with a cookie consent notice. By clicking 'Accept All', you consent to the use of all cookie categories described in this policy. You may also customise your preferences by selecting specific categories. Choosing 'Reject Non-Essential' will limit cookies to essential cookies only.
Your consent is stored and respected on subsequent visits. You may change your cookie preferences at any time by accessing the cookie settings panel available in the website footer.
4.7 Managing Cookies Through Browser Settings
Most web browsers allow you to manage cookie preferences through their settings. You can typically:
View all cookies stored by websites.
Delete individual or all cookies.
Block all cookies from specific websites.
Set preferences to be notified before a cookie is placed.
Please note that blocking essential cookies will impair your ability to use the Platform. Instructions for managing cookies in popular browsers can be found through the browser's help documentation. Clearing cookies will also remove any saved preferences or login sessions.
4.8 Third-Party Cookies
Some cookies on the Platform are set by third-party service providers, including analytics providers and social sharing tools. These third parties have their own privacy and cookie policies. Charitey does not control the cookies set by third parties and recommends that you review the relevant third-party policies. Currently, third-party cookies may be set by analytics services. We will maintain an updated list of third-party cookie providers in our Platform's cookie management interface.
4.9 Changes to This Cookie Policy
We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time to reflect changes in technology, regulation, or our Platform's features. Material changes will be communicated via the Platform and, where required, renewed consent will be sought. The 'Last Updated' date at the top of this document will reflect any changes.
