accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
paragraphs:
8. Accessibility Statement
Effective Date: 1 July 2025 | Last Updated: 1 July 2025
8.1 Accessibility Commitment
Charitey is committed to making its Platform accessible to all users, regardless of disability, age, assistive technology use, or level of digital literacy. We believe that social impact tools should be available to everyone, and we are dedicated to removing barriers that prevent people from participating in the Platform's charitable mission.
8.2 Standards
We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA as published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). These guidelines describe four key principles of accessible web design:
Perceivable: Information and user interface components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive.
Operable: User interface components and navigation must be operable.
Understandable: Information and the operation of the user interface must be understandable.
Robust: Content must be robust enough to be interpreted by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies.
8.3 Specific Accessibility Features
Charitey endeavours to implement the following accessibility features on the Platform:
Screen Reader Support: All key content, forms, buttons, and interactive elements are labelled to support screen reader software.
Keyboard Navigation: The Platform can be navigated using a keyboard alone, without requiring the use of a mouse.
Text Alternatives: Images, icons, and non-text elements include descriptive alternative text.
Colour Contrast: Text and background colours are selected to meet minimum contrast ratios.
Resizable Text: Text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality.
Form Accessibility: All forms include clear labels, instructions, and error messages.
Consistent Navigation: Navigation menus and structures are consistent across the Platform.
8.4 Limitations
While we strive to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA, Charitey is a new and evolving Platform. There may be areas where our current implementation falls short of these standards. We are actively working to identify and address any accessibility gaps and will prioritise improvements as part of our development roadmap.
8.5 Ongoing Improvements
Charitey's accessibility programme includes:
Regular accessibility audits of the Platform by our development team.
User testing with individuals who use assistive technologies.
Staff training on accessible design and content creation.
Scheduled reviews of this Accessibility Statement to reflect current Platform status.
Inclusion of accessibility considerations in the design and development of future features, including the planned mobile application.
8.6 Feedback
We welcome feedback from users about their accessibility experience on the Platform. If you encounter accessibility barriers or have suggestions for improvement, please contact us at:
Email: accessibility@charitey.org
Subject: Accessibility Feedback
We aim to acknowledge accessibility feedback within 5 business days and to provide a substantive response within 21 business days.

data-deletion-policy.title: Data Deletion Policy
paragraphs:
Effective Date: 31 August 2026 | Last Updated: 31 August 2026
Internal working draft — aligned to the current implemented application flow

This Data Deletion Policy explains how a Fourth Idly user may request deletion of their account and associated personal data, what information may be removed, what information may need to be retained, and the general processing sequence applicable to deletion requests.

This Policy is intended to be read together with the Fourth Idly Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions. It reflects the current application flow, including Donor, NGO, and Volunteer accounts; NGO and Volunteer verification documents; donations and Need Requests; delivery and payment records; notifications; chat; ratings; feedback; impact posts; and administrative dispute handling.
## 6.1 Account Deletion

Users may request deletion of their Fourth Idly account, subject to applicable law and any lawful retention requirements. Account deletion may be requested through any account-deletion functionality made available in the Platform or through the official privacy/support channel.

Where the application provides an Account Settings or Profile deletion option, the User may submit the request through that flow. Where no in-app deletion option is available for a particular account state or role, the User may contact Fourth Idly using the official privacy or support contact details published through the Platform.

Upon receiving a deletion request, Fourth Idly may verify the identity of the requester before initiating deletion in order to prevent unauthorised deletion or disclosure. If additional information is reasonably necessary to verify the requester, the User may be asked to provide it.

A deletion request does not automatically require immediate destruction of every record. Fourth Idly may first identify active data, transaction records, unresolved disputes, verification records, security records, and other information subject to lawful retention.
## 6.2 What Is Deleted

Subject to the exceptions described in this Policy, Fourth Idly will take reasonable steps to delete or anonymise personal data from active systems when it is no longer required for a lawful purpose. Depending on the User’s role and activity, this may include:
• Name, username, email address, phone number, location/profile information, and other ordinary profile information.
• Optional profile photograph.
• Account authentication/profile records that are no longer required after account closure, subject to security and legal retention requirements.
• Donor donation information associated with the User, where deletion is legally and operationally possible.
• NGO Need Requests and associated profile information, subject to transaction, audit, dispute, and legal retention requirements.
• Volunteer task, pickup, delivery, and associated profile information, subject to transaction, safety, audit, dispute, and legal retention requirements.
• Uploaded NGO licence/registration documents and Volunteer driving-licence documents, except where retention is required for a lawful purpose.
• Notification-related account/device-token information that is no longer required.
• Direct messages and Platform communications associated with the account, where deletion is legally and technically possible.
• Ratings and feedback associated with the account, subject to the need to preserve transaction integrity, fraud-prevention records, and information that must lawfully remain.
• Impact posts and other user-generated content, subject to the rights of other participants, transaction history, moderation, legal obligations, and technical retention requirements.
• Saved preferences and non-essential account settings.
• Other personal data that is no longer required for a lawful and documented purpose.

Deletion may not mean that every reference to an account disappears from historical records. For example, a completed donation, payment dispute, safety incident, or administrative action may require limited retention of records, potentially in de-identified or restricted form.
## 6.3 Donation, Need Request and Transaction Data

Fourth Idly facilitates interactions between Donors, NGOs, and Volunteers. Deleting an account may therefore affect records that involve other Users. Where a record is necessary to preserve the integrity of a completed donation, delivery, payment verification, rating, dispute, or administrative review, Fourth Idly may retain a limited record even after the requesting User’s account is closed.
• Need Request records may be retained where necessary to document fulfilment, expiry, cancellation, disputes, or Platform history.
• Donation records may be retained where necessary to establish what was offered, accepted, delivered, cancelled, or disputed.
• Delivery records may be retained where necessary to establish pickup, delivery, receipt, or safety-related events.
• Delivery Fee records may be retained where necessary to document payment status, payment verification, or a dispute.
• Payment reference information voluntarily submitted for dispute handling may be retained for as long as reasonably necessary for that dispute and any related legal or audit purpose.
• Ratings and feedback may require limited retention to preserve the integrity of the Platform’s transaction history and prevent manipulation.
## 6.4 NGO Verification Data

NGO onboarding may include a licence or registration ID and an uploaded licence/registration PDF. When an NGO requests account deletion, Fourth Idly will assess whether the verification document and related records can be deleted immediately.

Where a verification record is required to demonstrate the basis on which an organisation was approved, investigate fraud or abuse, resolve a dispute, comply with legal requirements, or protect the integrity of the Platform, Fourth Idly may retain the minimum necessary information for the applicable retention period.

The original Charitey policy specified a five-year retention period for NGO verification records. That specific period has not been carried forward as an automatic Fourth Idly rule because the current Fourth Idly application flow establishes the collection and verification of NGO documentation but does not, by itself, establish a five-year statutory retention requirement. Any fixed retention period should be confirmed against the final legal and regulatory requirements applicable to Fourth Idly.
## 6.5 Volunteer Verification Data
Volunteer onboarding may include a driving licence ID and an uploaded driving licence PDF. These documents are used for administrative verification and approval.

Following account deletion, Fourth Idly may delete the uploaded document when it is no longer necessary. However, limited verification or administrative records may be retained where required for legal compliance, fraud prevention, investigation of complaints, safety incidents, disputes, or audit. Any retention should be limited to what is reasonably necessary for the applicable purpose.
## 6.6 Delivery Fee and Payment Data

The current delivery flow may involve a Delivery Fee paid by a Donor to a Volunteer through UPI. The Platform may store the Volunteer’s UPI ID, applicable Delivery Fee amount, payment status, and a payment reference ID where supplied for verification or dispute handling.

Account deletion does not necessarily erase payment-related records immediately. Fourth Idly may retain limited payment and dispute information where necessary to establish the history of a transaction, resolve an outstanding dispute, prevent fraud, satisfy accounting/audit requirements, or comply with applicable law.

Fourth Idly does not intend to store a User’s UPI PIN, banking password, or banking OTP through the Platform. Information processed by a third-party UPI application is governed by that provider’s applicable policies.
## 6.7 Ratings, Feedback and Impact Posts

Where an account has participated in a completed donation, Users may have submitted or received ratings, feedback, or impact-post content. Deletion requests will be assessed in the context of those records.
• Profile information may be removed or anonymised where technically and legally appropriate.
• Ratings and review information may be retained in limited form where necessary to preserve transaction integrity or prevent fraudulent manipulation.
• Written feedback may be deleted where no lawful retention purpose applies, subject to the rights and records of other participants.
• Impact posts may be deleted or anonymised where appropriate, subject to content ownership, legal obligations, moderation requirements, and the involvement of other Users.
• Content required for an unresolved complaint, dispute, investigation, or legal obligation may be retained until the relevant matter is resolved.
## 6.8 Chat, Notifications and Device Data
When an account is deleted, Fourth Idly will take reasonable steps to remove account-linked notification tokens and other non-essential device information that is no longer required.

Chat and communication records may be deleted where legally and technically possible. However, selected records may need to be retained for security, fraud prevention, support, dispute resolution, legal compliance, or the protection of other Users.
Notification history and operational records may be retained for a limited period where necessary for audit, troubleshooting, delivery verification, payment disputes, or other lawful purposes.
## 6.9 Retention Period Before Active Deletion

The original Charitey policy stated fixed deletion periods of 30 days for active deletion and up to 90 additional days for backups. For Fourth Idly, these periods should be treated as operational targets only if they are adopted into the final internal retention schedule and supported by the actual storage and backup architecture.

Following a valid deletion request, Fourth Idly will initiate the deletion process within a reasonable period and in accordance with applicable law. The timing may depend on identity verification, account state, outstanding transactions, unresolved disputes, security investigations, technical deletion cycles, and lawful retention requirements.

Where a fixed service-level period is later adopted, this section should be updated to match the actual technical deletion and backup-retention capabilities rather than promising a period the infrastructure cannot reliably meet.
## 6.10 Backup Removal

Data deleted from active systems may remain temporarily in encrypted backups or disaster-recovery copies because backup systems are designed to preserve system integrity and recoverability. Such data will not ordinarily be restored for active processing except where necessary for disaster recovery, security, legal requirements, or other legitimate operational purposes.

Backup copies should be overwritten or securely purged according to Fourth Idly’s applicable backup-retention schedule. The exact period depends on the final infrastructure and backup configuration. If a fixed backup period is adopted, it should be stated consistently across this Policy, the Privacy Policy, and Fourth Idly’s internal data-retention schedule.
## 6.11 Legal Exceptions to Deletion
Fourth Idly may retain certain personal data beyond the ordinary deletion process where retention is necessary or permitted under applicable law. Examples include:
• Compliance with applicable Indian legal or regulatory obligations.
• Responding to lawful government, court, law-enforcement, or regulatory requests.
• Resolving pending or reasonably anticipated legal disputes, claims, or complaints.
• Maintaining records required for accounting, tax, audit, or other lawful reporting purposes.
• Preventing, detecting, investigating, or documenting fraud, abuse, payment manipulation, or serious security incidents.
• Maintaining records necessary to enforce Platform Terms and protect the rights, safety, property, or security of Fourth Idly and other Users.
• Preserving evidence relating to an unresolved dispute or investigation.
• Maintaining limited transaction history where deletion would materially undermine the integrity of records involving other Users.

Where information is retained under a legal or other lawful exception, Fourth Idly will seek to limit the retained information to what is reasonably necessary and will not use retained information for unrelated purposes except where permitted by applicable law.
## 6.12 Blocked or Banned Accounts

If an account has been permanently blocked or banned for serious misconduct, fraud, abuse, payment manipulation, document fraud, or other prohibited conduct, Fourth Idly may retain limited information necessary to prevent the User from circumventing the restriction and creating a new account.

Such retention will be limited to the extent reasonably necessary for fraud prevention, platform security, enforcement, or legal compliance and will be handled in accordance with the Privacy Policy and applicable law.
## 6.13 Identity Verification for Deletion Requests
Because account deletion is an irreversible action that may affect personal data and transaction history, Fourth Idly may require reasonable identity verification before processing the request.
• The requester may be asked to authenticate through the account where available.
• Additional verification may be requested if the request originates outside the authenticated account or if suspicious activity is detected.
• Fourth Idly will avoid requesting unnecessary sensitive information solely for identity verification.
• Where identity cannot reasonably be verified, Fourth Idly may delay or reject the deletion request to protect the account holder and other Users.
## 6.14 Deletion of Data Shared with Other Users

Some Platform data is shared as part of the donation and delivery workflow. For example, an NGO Need Request may have been viewed by Donors, and delivery information may have been shared with a Volunteer. Deleting a User’s account does not necessarily require Fourth Idly to erase records that another User is independently entitled or required to retain.

Fourth Idly will nevertheless take reasonable steps to minimise unnecessary personal information in retained records and, where technically and legally appropriate, may anonymise or pseudonymise historical records.
## 6.15 Effect of Account Deletion

After an account is deleted, the User may lose access to the Platform and to historical information associated with that account, including donation history, Need Requests, task history, ratings, feedback, messages, and other account features.

Deletion does not cancel or reverse a completed donation, delivery, payment, rating, dispute, or other transaction that has already occurred. Where an outstanding obligation or dispute exists, Fourth Idly may retain limited information until the matter is appropriately resolved.
## 6.16 Processing Timeline Summary
The deletion process generally follows these stages:
• Stage 1 — Request received: Fourth Idly receives an account/data deletion request through an available authorised channel.
• Stage 2 — Verification: The identity and authority of the requester may be verified.
• Stage 3 — Account restriction/deactivation: Where appropriate, the account may be deactivated or access restricted while deletion is processed.
• Stage 4 — Active-data review: Fourth Idly identifies personal data that can be deleted and information that is subject to lawful retention.
• Stage 5 — Active deletion/anonymisation: Deletable information is removed or anonymised from active systems.
• Stage 6 — Backup lifecycle: Deleted information may remain temporarily in encrypted backups until those backups expire or are securely purged according to the applicable backup schedule.
• Stage 7 — Retained records: Information subject to a legal, security, audit, dispute, or fraud-prevention exception remains restricted and is used only for the applicable lawful purpose.
• Stage 8 — Completion: The deletion request is treated as completed when the applicable active-system deletion process has finished, subject to lawful retained records and technical backup cycles.
The exact duration of each stage depends on the account type, the data involved, outstanding transactions or disputes, and the final Fourth Idly technical retention schedule.
## 6.17 Requesting Deletion of Specific Data

A User may also ask Fourth Idly to delete a specific category of personal data without deleting the entire account, where such functionality or request is legally available. Examples may include a profile photograph, optional content, or other information that is no longer necessary.

Fourth Idly may decline or limit a specific deletion request where the information is necessary for account security, a current transaction, dispute resolution, legal compliance, or another lawful purpose.
## 6.18 Data Deletion and Privacy Rights

This Policy should be read together with the Fourth Idly Privacy Policy, which describes the broader rights available to Users regarding access, correction, deletion, consent withdrawal, grievance redressal, and other data-protection rights. If applicable law provides a different requirement from this Policy, the applicable law will prevail to the extent of the conflict.
## 6.19 Policy Updates

Fourth Idly may update this Data Deletion Policy when the Platform, storage architecture, backup systems, legal requirements, or deletion mechanisms change. The effective date and last-updated date will be revised when material changes are made.
The deletion periods described in this Policy should remain consistent with Fourth Idly’s actual technical capabilities and internal data-retention schedule.
## 6.20 Contact for Data Deletion

For account deletion requests, data deletion enquiries, or privacy-related assistance, Users should use the official privacy/support contact details published by Fourth Idly through the Platform or its official communications.

The final official Fourth Idly privacy/grievance email address and postal/contact details should be inserted here once confirmed. The Charitey email addresses from the source document have intentionally not been carried over.
## 6.21 Acknowledgement

By submitting a deletion request, the User acknowledges that account deletion may be irreversible and may result in loss of access to Platform services and historical account information. The User further acknowledges that Fourth Idly may retain limited information where required or permitted by applicable law, for unresolved transactions or disputes, fraud prevention, security, audit, or other lawful purposes.

data-collection-permission-policy.title: Data Collection & Permission Policy
paragraphs:
Effective Date: 31 August 2026 | Last Updated: 31 August 2026
Full-length version — aligned to the current implemented application flow

This Data Collection and Permission Policy explains what information Fourth Idly collects through its current mobile application, why that information is required, which device permissions may be requested, how role-specific information is used, and how Users can control permissions through their device settings.

This Policy is based on the current implemented Fourth Idly application flow. It should be read together with the Fourth Idly Privacy Policy, Terms and Conditions, Community Guidelines, Data Deletion Policy, and other applicable Platform policies.

Fourth Idly follows a data-minimisation approach: information and permissions should be requested only when reasonably necessary for an identified Platform function. A permission should not be treated as consent to collect unrelated information.
## 10.1 Scope

This Policy applies to Donors, NGOs, Volunteers, and other authorised Users who access the Fourth Idly mobile application and its connected services. It covers information entered by Users, information generated through Platform activity, and information processed through supported device or application services.

The current application uses Flutter on mobile, Firebase Authentication for email/password and phone OTP authentication, Cloud Firestore for real-time application data, Firebase Storage for profile photographs and verification documents, Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for push notifications, and UPI deep links/QR generation for Delivery Fee payments.
## 10.2 User Roles and Data Collection
Fourth Idly uses role-based onboarding. Users first select one of three available roles — Donor, NGO, or Volunteer — and the information collected after role selection depends on the selected role.

• Donor: common account and profile information is collected to enable browsing of NGO requests, creating donations, coordinating delivery where applicable, paying the Delivery Fee, and rating the Volunteer.
• NGO: common account information plus NGO licence/registration information and a supporting licence/registration PDF are collected for verification before the account is activated.

• Volunteer: common account information plus driving licence information, a driving licence PDF, UPI ID, and optionally vehicle type are collected for verification, task assignment, delivery coordination, and Delivery Fee payment.

• Admin: administrators use a separate web panel to approve, reject, block, manage donations and deliveries, resolve disputes, review ratings/feedback, view notifications, and access audit information. The public mobile onboarding flow does not create an Admin account.
## 10.3 Information Collected From All Registered Users
The current onboarding flow collects the following common account information:
• Email address — required for account authentication and account communication.
• Password — supplied during registration and handled through Firebase Authentication; Fourth Idly does not intend to store a plaintext password in the application database.
• Name — used for account identity and relevant Platform interactions.
• Username — a unique handle used to identify the User within the Platform.
• Location — entered as text or map-area information and used to support donation and delivery coordination.
• Phone number — used as part of the phone OTP verification process.
• Phone verification status — records whether the phone verification step has been completed.
• Profile photograph — optional and uploaded to Platform storage when the User chooses to provide one.
• Role — records whether the account is a Donor, NGO, or Volunteer.
• Account status — may be pending, approved, active, rejected, or blocked depending on the role and administrative process.
• Rating information — average rating and total review count may be maintained where the User receives eligible ratings.
## 10.4 Authentication and Account Permissions

The current application uses email/password authentication followed by phone OTP verification during onboarding. This means the application needs access to information necessary to create, authenticate, and maintain the User account.

Phone OTP verification may involve sending and receiving a verification code through the supported authentication service. Users should never share an OTP with another person or enter an OTP into an unauthorised application.

Authentication permission or access does not give Fourth Idly permission to read unrelated phone contents, contacts, messages, or other device information unless a separate feature explicitly requests and receives the relevant device permission.
## 10.5 NGO-Specific Data Collection
NGOs are subject to administrative verification. The current flow collects:
• Licence or registration ID.
• Licence/registration PDF uploaded by the NGO.
• NGO account status, including pending, approved/active, rejected, or blocked states.
• Information contained in the Need Requests created by the NGO, such as request type, quantity, unit, description, required-by date/time, volunteer preference, and optional pickup location.

The licence/registration PDF is stored in Firebase Storage through the current implementation and is made available for the authorised verification process. Users must submit documents only where they have lawful authority to do so.
## 10.6 Volunteer-Specific Data Collection
Volunteers are subject to administrative verification. The current flow collects:
• Driving licence ID.
• Driving licence PDF uploaded for verification.
• UPI ID used to generate the payment destination for Delivery Fees.
• Vehicle type, where the Volunteer chooses to provide it.
• Task, pickup, delivery, and payment-verification information generated through Volunteer activity.
• Rating information received from eligible interactions.

The driving licence information is collected for the implemented Volunteer verification process. UPI ID is collected so that the application can construct the UPI payment destination and QR/deep link for the applicable Delivery Fee.
## 10.7 Donor-Specific Data Collection
Donors use the common account/profile information and generate additional information through donation activity.
• Donation item type and description.
• Donation quantity and related donation information.
• Selected NGO and donation relationship.
• Donation status and delivery status.
• Delivery Fee information where applicable.
• Payment status and, where supplied for a dispute, payment reference information.
• Volunteer rating and optional feedback after payment verification.
• Donation history and related impact information displayed in the User profile.
## 10.8 NGO Need Request Data
When an NGO creates a Need Request, the current application may collect and store:
• Request type: Food or Product.
• Quantity.
• Unit.
• Description.
• Required-by date and time, stored as the request's liveUntil value.
• Volunteer preference: 'I have volunteer' or 'Need platform volunteer'.
• Optional pickup map pin, including pickup latitude, pickup longitude, and pickup address when the NGO chooses to provide it.
• Request status, including open, expired, or fulfilled-related states.
• Fulfilled quantity and related donation information.
Need Request information is used to show eligible open requests to Donors and to coordinate the resulting donation and delivery workflow.
## 10.9 Donation and Delivery Data

When a Donor makes a donation, the application creates a donation record. The current data model may contain information needed to connect the Donor, NGO, item, quantity, Volunteer assignment, delivery stages, payment state, and rating state.
• Donor and NGO identifiers.
• Item and quantity information.
• Donation status.
• Volunteer assignment or acceptance information where a platform Volunteer is used.
• Pickup and delivery state.
• Payment status and applicable Delivery Fee.
• Volunteer UPI information required for the payment screen.
• Payment verification or dispute state.
• Optional payment reference ID supplied by the Donor for dispute handling.
• Rating and feedback fields generated after eligible completion.
## 10.10 Location and Map Information
The current NGO Need Request flow allows an NGO to provide an optional pickup map pin. Where the NGO uses this function, the application may collect:
• Pickup latitude.
• Pickup longitude.
• Pickup address.
• Location information entered by the User in the general profile.

The current technical flow does not establish continuous background GPS tracking as part of the standard donation workflow. Accordingly, this Policy does not represent that Fourth Idly continuously tracks a Volunteer’s live location.

If a future version introduces continuous or foreground location tracking, the application should request the relevant operating-system permission at the point of need and this Policy should be updated before that feature is introduced.
## 10.11 Profile Photo and File Uploads
Profile photographs are optional. When a User chooses to upload one, the selected image is stored through Firebase Storage and associated with the User profile.

NGO and Volunteer verification PDFs are also uploaded to Firebase Storage. These documents are distinct from optional profile photographs and are collected for role-specific administrative verification.

Fourth Idly should not request access to a User's entire photo library merely to create an account. Where the operating system presents a file or photo picker, the User may select the specific image or document intended for upload.
## 10.12 Device Permissions Overview

Device permissions are controls provided by the mobile operating system. A permission is requested when a Platform feature requires access to a protected device capability. Granting a permission does not automatically mean that Fourth Idly will collect every type of information available through that capability.

Based on the current implementation, the principal permission-sensitive functions are notifications, optional map/location input, profile/document uploads, and QR image download to the device gallery.

• Notifications — Deliver donation, volunteer, delivery, payment, message, expiry, task, rating and dispute-related notifications through FCM. Optional at device level, but useful for timely workflow updates. Can be allowed or denied through device notification settings.

• Location / Map Access — Support an optional pickup map pin when the relevant location feature is used. Optional based on the feature; the current NGO pickup pin is optional. Can be denied; the User may instead provide available location/address information where supported.

• Photos / File Selection — Upload an optional profile photo and role-specific verification PDFs. Only when the User chooses to upload relevant content. Controlled through the operating system picker/permission mechanism.

• Gallery / Media Save — Save the generated Delivery Fee QR image to the device gallery when the User chooses the download action. Optional; only needed for the save-to-gallery action. User chooses whether to save the generated QR.
• Camera — No camera-based collection is established in the current technical flow. Not required by the documented current flow. Should not be requested unless a future camera feature is introduced.

• Contacts — No contact-list collection is established in the current technical flow. Not required by the documented current flow. Should not be requested unless a future feature specifically requires it.

• Microphone — No microphone-based collection is established in the current technical flow. Not required by the documented current flow. Should not be requested unless a future voice feature is introduced.
## 10.13 Push Notification Permission

Fourth Idly uses Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for push notifications. The current implementation saves an FCM token on the User document so that relevant notifications can be delivered to the correct device/account.
Notifications may relate to:
• Donation offers.
• Volunteer acceptance.
• New chat messages.
• Post tags.
• Donation cancellations.
• Expired Need Requests.
• Delivery arrival.
• Payment pending.
• Payment verification.
• Payment verification completion.
• New Volunteer tasks.
• Urgent Volunteer tasks.
• Payment rejection or dispute status.

Push notification permission is controlled by the device operating system. If a User denies notifications, the User may not receive timely push alerts, but the in-app notification system may still contain relevant notifications when the User opens the application.

The current flow is operational/transactional rather than a documented marketing-notification system. Any future marketing notification programme should be separately disclosed and, where required, based on appropriate consent.
## 10.14 Location Permission and Optional Pickup Pin

Location-related access is intended to support the donation logistics workflow rather than continuous surveillance. The current Need Request screen allows the NGO to choose whether to provide a pickup map pin.

If the application requests location permission to support map selection or location services, the permission should be requested in context, with a clear explanation of why it is needed. If the User declines, Fourth Idly should not treat the denial as permission to obtain location through another unauthorised method.
The current technical specification identifies pickupLat, pickupLng, and pickupAddress as optional Need Request fields. It does not establish continuous background location collection.
## 10.15 Photo, Document and Storage Permission
The current Platform uses Firebase Storage for profile photographs and licence PDFs. The User initiates the upload by selecting the relevant file or photograph.
• Profile photo upload is optional.
• NGO licence/registration PDF upload is role-specific and used for verification.
• Volunteer driving licence PDF upload is role-specific and used for verification.
• Users should select only the document or image intended for the Platform.
• Fourth Idly should not use uploaded documents for unrelated purposes outside the purposes described in the Privacy Policy and applicable policies.
## 10.16 QR Code Generation and Gallery Access
When a Delivery Fee applies, the current Donor payment screen loads the Volunteer UPI ID and applicable fee amount, constructs a UPI URI, and generates a scannable QR code.

The current implementation provides a function to download the generated QR image to the device gallery. This is a User-initiated action and is separate from collecting the User's personal gallery contents.

Fourth Idly does not need to read unrelated photographs merely because the User chooses to save the generated QR image. The relevant operating-system media/storage behaviour will depend on the device and operating-system version.
## 10.17 UPI and Payment Information

Fourth Idly facilitates a Delivery Fee payment from the Donor to the Volunteer where the delivery workflow requires one. The current application uses a UPI deep link and QR code rather than a conventional in-app card or banking credential form.
The application may process:
• Volunteer UPI ID.
• Delivery Fee amount.
• UPI URI parameters required to construct the payment destination.
• Payment status.
• Payment verification state.
• Optional payment reference ID supplied for a dispute.

The current technical flow explicitly states that the application does not store UPI PINs, banking passwords, or banking OTPs. Users should never disclose such credentials to Fourth Idly, another User, or anyone claiming to represent Fourth Idly.
Processing performed by an external UPI application is governed by that provider's own terms and privacy practices.
## 10.18 Chat and Communication Data

The current application includes chat associated with donation and Volunteer workflows. Chat rooms and messages are stored as Platform data so that relevant participants can communicate about the donation, Volunteer acceptance, pickup, delivery, and related matters.
• Message content.
• Sender and recipient identifiers.
• Relevant chat-room or donation/task relationship.
• Message timestamps.
• Notification information generated from new messages.
Users should not use chat to share passwords, OTPs, UPI PINs, banking passwords, or unnecessary sensitive personal information.
## 10.19 Ratings and Feedback Data
The current Platform records ratings generated from completed donation interactions.
• Donor → Volunteer: star rating and optional text feedback.
• NGO → Donor: rating.
• NGO → Volunteer: rating where a Volunteer participated.
• Average rating and total review count may be updated on the relevant User profile.
• An Admin may view live ratings and feedback through the administrative Feedbacks page.
• Legacy app-survey feedback may also exist in the feedbacks collection.
Ratings and feedback are collected to support trust, quality, dispute review, and community accountability. They should be based on genuine Platform interactions.
## 10.20 Impact Posts and Community Content

Following completion, the current flow encourages or directs eligible NGOs to create an impact post. Such posts may contain text, photographs, and information describing the social impact of a completed donation.

Content submitted through impact posts is User-generated data and may be displayed through relevant Platform surfaces. Users should obtain appropriate permission before posting identifiable images or personal information concerning beneficiaries or other individuals.
## 10.21 Notification and In-App Activity Data
The current in-app notification system is backed by Firestore and may store information such as:
• Notification ID.
• Receiver ID.
• Sender ID and sender name where applicable.
• Notification type.
• Title and message.
• Related donation, task, post, or other item ID.
• Read/unread state.
• Creation timestamp.
Notifications are marked as read when the User taps the relevant notification according to the current implementation.
## 10.22 Administrative and Security Data
The Admin web panel supports User approval, rejection, blocking, donation and delivery management, dispute resolution, ratings/feedback review, notifications, audit logs, and settings.

Accordingly, Fourth Idly may maintain administrative information necessary to determine account status, review NGO/Volunteer verification, investigate payment disputes, manage donations and deliveries, protect Platform integrity, and document administrative actions.

Administrative access should be restricted according to role and operational need. Users do not receive access to internal administrative information merely because that information relates to their account.
## 10.23 Data Storage and Processing Services
The current technical implementation uses the following principal services:
• Firebase Authentication — email/password authentication and phone OTP verification.
• Cloud Firestore — real-time storage for Users, Need Requests, Donations, notifications, posts, feedback, and related Platform records.
• Firebase Storage — profile photographs and NGO/Volunteer verification PDFs.
• Firebase Cloud Messaging — push notification delivery and FCM device tokens.
• UPI deep links and QR generation — construction and presentation of Delivery Fee payment instructions.
The use of these services means that relevant information is processed by the applicable service infrastructure. Third-party processing is addressed in the Fourth Idly Privacy Policy.
## 10.24 What Fourth Idly Does Not Collect Through the Current Flow

The current technical flow does not establish collection of several categories that were present in the older Charitey policy or may commonly be associated with other applications. Unless a future feature is introduced and separately disclosed, Fourth Idly does not represent that it collects:
• Date of birth as a standard onboarding field.
• Gender as a standard onboarding field.
• Emergency contact information as a standard onboarding field.
• Google Sign-In data as part of the documented current authentication flow.
• Continuous background GPS location.
• Contact-list contents.
• Microphone recordings.
• UPI PINs.
• Banking passwords.
• Banking OTPs.
• Full device photo-library contents simply because an image is uploaded.
• Corporate affiliation, FCRA details, 80G/12A certificates, or bank account details as standard current NGO onboarding fields.
This list is intended to distinguish the current implemented flow from the broader and more generic information categories contained in the older Charitey privacy materials.
## 10.25 Permission Denial and Feature Availability

Users may deny an optional device permission. Denial may limit a feature that depends on that permission but should not, by itself, authorise Fourth Idly to obtain the information through an alternative method.
• If notifications are denied, timely push alerts may not appear on the device.
• If location access is denied, a map-based location feature may be unavailable or the User may need to provide the supported location/address information manually.
• If photo/file access is not granted, the User may be unable to upload a selected profile photo or verification document until the relevant file-selection mechanism is permitted.
• If gallery/media access is unavailable, saving the generated QR image may not work; this does not affect the underlying UPI payment information itself.
## 10.26 Permission Changes

Users can generally review or change application permissions through their device settings. The exact menu names and controls vary by Android version, device manufacturer, and operating-system configuration.

Changing a permission does not necessarily delete information that was previously provided to Fourth Idly. Data deletion is governed by the Fourth Idly Data Deletion Policy and applicable privacy rights.
Where a permission is no longer necessary for a feature, Fourth Idly should not continue requesting it solely because it was previously granted.
## 10.27 Data Minimisation

Fourth Idly is designed around a defined donation and delivery workflow. The Platform should collect only the information reasonably necessary to provide the relevant function, maintain account security, coordinate donations, support delivery, verify role-specific accounts, process Delivery Fee verification, provide notifications, support ratings, resolve disputes, and comply with applicable obligations.

Optional information should remain optional unless a legitimate Platform function requires it. A User should not be required to provide unrelated personal information merely to access a feature that does not need it.
## 10.28 Consent and User Choice

Where the Platform requests a device permission, the User makes the permission decision through the operating system. Where information is optional and entered directly by the User, the User may choose whether to provide it unless it is required for the relevant feature or legal obligation.

Where processing depends on consent, the applicable consent mechanism should clearly identify the purpose of the processing. Withdrawal of consent should not affect the lawfulness of processing that occurred before withdrawal.
## 10.29 Children and Age-Related Use

The current Fourth Idly policy framework should define the minimum age and any applicable parental or guardian requirements consistently across the Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, and this Policy. The current technical flow document does not specify an age field in onboarding.

Until the final legal position is confirmed, Fourth Idly should not request a date of birth merely because an older policy contained one. Any age verification mechanism introduced later should be separately documented and implemented only where necessary.
## 10.30 Security and Permission Protection

Permissions and collected data should be protected through the security controls applicable to the Platform and its infrastructure. Access to verification documents, payment-dispute information, account records, and administrative data should be limited to authorised functions.
• Authentication is handled through Firebase Authentication.
• Verification PDFs and profile photographs are stored through Firebase Storage.
• Application records are stored through Cloud Firestore with appropriate access controls.
• FCM tokens are used for notification routing and should not be treated as general device-identification data.
• Sensitive banking credentials such as UPI PINs, banking passwords, and OTPs are not stored by the current application flow.
## 10.31 Retention and Deletion
Data collected through permissions or Platform features is subject to the retention principles described in the Fourth Idly Privacy Policy and Data Deletion Policy.

Deleting a permission from the device is not the same as deleting data already stored by Fourth Idly. Users who want stored personal data deleted should use the applicable account/data deletion process.

Certain records may be retained where necessary for unresolved disputes, fraud prevention, security, administrative accountability, legal obligations, or the integrity of transaction records, as described in the Data Deletion Policy.
## 10.32 Changes to the Data Collection and Permission Policy

Fourth Idly may update this Policy when the application introduces a new permission-sensitive feature, changes its authentication or storage architecture, adds new categories of personal data, changes notification functionality, or becomes subject to new legal or platform requirements.
Material changes should be reflected in the application permission prompts and the Privacy Policy so that Users are not asked to grant permissions for purposes that are not clearly disclosed.
## 10.33 Contact and Privacy Enquiries

Questions concerning data collection, device permissions, personal information, or privacy should be directed to the official Fourth Idly privacy/support contact details published through the Platform.
The final official Fourth Idly privacy and grievance email addresses should be inserted here once confirmed. Legacy Charitey contact addresses have intentionally not been carried over.
## 10.34 Summary of Current Permission Position

For clarity, the current Fourth Idly application is primarily a donation logistics platform. Its core data collection is account information, role-specific verification information, donation and Need Request information, delivery and payment-verification information, notifications, ratings/feedback, chat, and optional community/impact content.

The current documented permission-sensitive functions are push notifications, optional map/location selection, user-initiated image/document upload, and saving a generated payment QR image to the device gallery. Camera, microphone, contact-list access, and continuous background location are not established by the current technical flow and should not be presented as current required permissions without a corresponding product change.

Fourth Idly respects the intellectual property rights of creators, organisations, Users, and other rights holders. This Copyright Policy explains ownership of Fourth Idly’s Platform materials, rights in User-generated content, the process for reporting suspected copyright infringement, the process for responding to a valid counter-notice, and Fourth Idly’s approach to repeat infringement.

This Policy applies to content and materials made available through the Fourth Idly mobile application and related Platform services, including Need Requests, Donation information, profile materials, chat, ratings, feedback, photographs, impact posts, NGO documentation, Volunteer documentation, and other content submitted or displayed through the Platform. It should be read together with the Fourth Idly Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, Community Guidelines, and Data Deletion Policy.
## 9.1 Ownership of Platform Content

All intellectual property rights in the Fourth Idly Platform — including the software, application interface, design, layout, original written content, logos, graphics, icons, visual elements, trademarks, service marks, and other original materials created or licensed for Fourth Idly — are owned by Fourth Idly or its licensors, to the extent applicable.

Such materials may be protected under the Copyright Act, 1957 (India), the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and other applicable intellectual-property laws. Unauthorised reproduction, distribution, public display, modification, adaptation, reverse engineering, extraction, or commercial exploitation of Fourth Idly’s protected materials is prohibited except where expressly authorised by Fourth Idly or permitted by applicable law.
• Do not copy or reproduce Fourth Idly’s application screens, original written materials, graphics, logos, or other protected content for a competing service without permission.
• Do not remove copyright, trademark, attribution, or other proprietary notices from Platform materials.
• Do not use the Fourth Idly name, logo, branding, or other marks in a way that suggests sponsorship, endorsement, affiliation, or authorisation without permission.
• Do not sell, license, redistribute, or commercially exploit Fourth Idly’s proprietary Platform materials without appropriate authorisation.
• Do not reproduce substantial portions of the Platform or its content through scraping, mirroring, systematic copying, or similar methods.
Nothing in this Policy prevents lawful uses that cannot legally be restricted, including applicable statutory exceptions, fair dealing or other permitted uses under Indian law.
## 9.2 User-Generated Content

Users may submit content to Fourth Idly in connection with Platform activity. Depending on the current application flow, this may include photographs, NGO activity or impact reports, Need Request descriptions, donation descriptions, profile photographs, ratings, feedback, chat messages, and other community content.

Users retain ownership of original content they create and have rights in, subject to the rights of third parties and any applicable licences. By submitting content to Fourth Idly, you grant Fourth Idly a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide licence, to the extent necessary, to host, store, reproduce, display, format, adapt, transmit, and otherwise use that content in connection with operating, providing, securing, moderating, improving, and promoting the Platform, subject to applicable law and the Privacy Policy.

This licence does not transfer ownership of the User’s underlying copyright. It is intended to allow Fourth Idly to perform the functions for which the content was submitted, including displaying a Need Request to relevant Donors, showing relevant delivery information to participants, displaying ratings or impact posts, storing content in Platform infrastructure, and maintaining records necessary for safety, support, moderation, and dispute resolution.
Users represent and warrant that:
• You are the original creator of the content or have all necessary rights, permissions, and licences to submit it.
• The content does not infringe copyright, trademark, privacy, publicity, moral rights, or other rights of a third party.
• You are authorised to grant the licence described in this Policy.
• Any identifiable person appearing in photographs, videos, or other content has been treated in accordance with applicable privacy, consent, and legal requirements.
• The content is not knowingly false, fraudulent, unlawful, defamatory, harassing, hateful, or otherwise prohibited by the Fourth Idly Community Guidelines or Terms and Conditions.

Users should be especially careful when uploading photographs or impact content involving beneficiaries, children, NGO staff, Donors, Volunteers, or other identifiable individuals. Appropriate consent or lawful authority should be obtained where required.
### 9.2.1 Content Submitted Through Current Platform Features
The current Fourth Idly flow may allow Users to submit or generate content through several features:
• NGO Need Requests may contain item descriptions, quantities, required-by dates/times, pickup information, and other descriptive content.
• Donation records may contain descriptions or information concerning offered food or products.
• Profile photographs may be uploaded by Users as optional profile content.

• NGO licence/registration PDFs and Volunteer driving-licence PDFs may be uploaded for administrative verification. These documents are primarily verification records and may contain third-party rights; Users must have lawful authority to submit them.
• Chat messages are User-generated communications and should not contain copyrighted material that the User has no right to share.
• Ratings and written feedback are User-generated content and must be truthful, relevant, and lawful.
• Impact posts may contain photographs, captions, activity descriptions, or other material intended to communicate social impact.

Fourth Idly may process and display such content according to the relevant Platform workflow. The fact that content can technically be uploaded does not mean that the User has permission to upload material owned by another person.
## 9.3 Copyright Complaints

Fourth Idly respects intellectual-property rights and takes credible copyright complaints seriously. If you believe that content available through the Platform infringes your copyright, you may submit a written copyright complaint using the official Fourth Idly copyright or legal contact channel.

Fourth Idly may review a sufficiently detailed complaint and, where appropriate, restrict access to, remove, disable, or otherwise address allegedly infringing content. Fourth Idly may also contact the relevant User or request additional information where necessary to assess the complaint.

A copyright complaint should be made by the copyright owner or an authorised representative. Knowingly submitting a false or materially misleading infringement complaint may result in appropriate action.
## 9.4 Reporting Copyright Infringement

To file a copyright complaint, please send a written notice to Fourth Idly’s official copyright/legal contact address published by the Platform. A useful and complete notice should contain the following information:
• A description of the copyrighted work that you claim has been infringed, including enough information to identify the work.

• A description of the material that you believe is infringing and its location on the Platform, such as a URL, post identifier, listing identifier, profile, screenshot, or other platform-specific identifier.
• Your full name and sufficient contact information, such as postal address, email address, and phone number, to allow Fourth Idly to contact you regarding the complaint.
• A statement that you have a good-faith belief that the disputed use is not authorised by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
• A statement that the information in your notice is accurate and that you are the copyright owner or authorised to act on the copyright owner’s behalf.
• An electronic or physical signature of the copyright owner or authorised representative.

Where possible, the complainant should also provide evidence supporting ownership or authority, such as a registration record, original publication information, licence documentation, or other material reasonably demonstrating the claimed right.

Fourth Idly will review valid and sufficiently detailed complaints as reasonably practicable. Depending on the circumstances, appropriate action may include removal or restriction of the reported content, contacting the submitting User, requesting clarification, or taking no action where the complaint is unsupported or the use appears lawful.
The handling of copyright complaints is subject to applicable Indian law, including the Copyright Act, 1957, and any other applicable legal requirements.
## 9.5 Counter Notice

If content submitted by you has been removed, restricted, or disabled following a copyright complaint and you believe the action resulted from mistake, misidentification, or another lawful basis for the content’s use, you may contact Fourth Idly through the official copyright/legal contact channel to request review.
A counter-notice should include:
• Identification of the removed or restricted content and its former location on the Platform.
• A statement explaining why you believe the content was removed or restricted by mistake or misidentification.
• Your full name and contact details sufficient for Fourth Idly to communicate with you.
• Information supporting your right to use the content, such as an ownership statement, licence, permission, public-domain basis, or other applicable legal exception.
• A statement that the information provided is accurate to the best of your knowledge.
• Your electronic or physical signature.
Where applicable and legally required, a counter-notice may also need to include consent to the jurisdiction of the appropriate court or other information required by applicable law.

Fourth Idly may review the counter-notice and the original complaint and may request additional information. Restoration of content is not automatic and may depend on the applicable law, the evidence received, the rights of the parties, and whether Fourth Idly is required or permitted to take further action.
Nothing in this section limits any rights or remedies available to a copyright owner or User under applicable law.
## 9.6 Repeat Infringers
Fourth Idly may take stronger action against Users who are found to be repeat infringers of intellectual-property rights.
• Repeatedly submitting content that is found to infringe another person’s copyright or other intellectual-property rights.
• Repeatedly uploading content after receiving credible notices concerning the same or substantially similar infringement.
• Using multiple accounts to continue uploading infringing content after a restriction or termination.
• Knowingly circumventing content restrictions imposed following legitimate copyright complaints.

Depending on the circumstances and applicable law, Fourth Idly may remove or restrict content, issue warnings, suspend particular features, suspend an account, block an account, or terminate access to the Platform.

Fourth Idly reserves the right to determine, based on the available evidence and circumstances, whether a User has engaged in repeated infringement. This determination will be made subject to applicable law and any rights available to the User.
## 9.7 Third-Party Materials and Licences

Users may encounter third-party materials through the Platform, including photographs, logos, product descriptions, organisation names, documents, maps, payment-related interfaces, and other content supplied by other Users or third-party services.

Fourth Idly does not automatically acquire ownership of third-party content merely because it is displayed or processed through the Platform. Users must respect the rights of the relevant copyright owners and licensors.
• Do not download, reproduce, modify, or commercially exploit third-party content merely because it is visible in the application.
• Do not use an NGO’s logo, photograph, report, or other protected material outside the scope of your lawful use.
• Do not upload third-party photographs, reports, artwork, documents, or other materials unless you have permission or another lawful basis.
• Do not assume that material found online is free to copy.
## 9.8 Copyright in NGO and Verification Documents

NGO licence/registration documents and Volunteer driving-licence documents may contain protected text, images, government marks, signatures, or other intellectual property belonging to the issuing organisation, authority, or individual.

These documents are collected for verification purposes within the Platform. Users must not copy, publish, distribute, or repurpose such documents outside the legitimate verification or Platform purpose without lawful authority.

Fourth Idly may store and process uploaded documents in its designated cloud infrastructure for verification, security, administration, dispute handling, and other lawful purposes described in the Privacy Policy.
## 9.9 Copyright and Impact Posts

Impact posts can include photographs, captions, reports, graphics, or other creative material. Users submitting such posts are responsible for ensuring that the material can lawfully be used by Fourth Idly for the Platform purposes described in this Policy.
• Obtain appropriate permission before using another person’s photograph where required.
• Do not copy another organisation’s impact report, photograph, campaign material, or written story and present it as your own.
• Do not remove attribution or copyright notices from third-party material.
• Do not upload stock photographs or internet images as if they depict an actual Fourth Idly donation or beneficiary unless you have the appropriate rights and clearly present them accurately.
• Do not manipulate or fabricate impact material in a way that misrepresents the underlying donation or event.
## 9.10 Copyright and Chat, Ratings and Feedback

Chat, ratings, and feedback are intended for communication and Platform participation. Users should not use these features to reproduce substantial copyrighted works that they do not have permission to share.

Short quotations or references may be lawful in some circumstances, but Users are responsible for determining whether their particular use is authorised or legally permitted. Fourth Idly may remove content that violates the Terms and Conditions, Community Guidelines, applicable law, or a valid intellectual-property complaint.
## 9.11 Platform Branding and Trademarks

The Fourth Idly name, logo, visual identity, slogans, and other branding elements may constitute trademarks or other protected intellectual property. Users may not use Fourth Idly branding in a manner that implies an unauthorised partnership, sponsorship, endorsement, certification, or official representation.

NGOs, Donors, Volunteers, and other community participants may refer to Fourth Idly factually when describing their participation, provided the reference does not mislead others about affiliation or endorsement.
## 9.12 Lawful Exceptions and User Rights

Nothing in this Copyright Policy is intended to remove rights that Users or rights holders have under applicable copyright law. Indian copyright law may permit certain uses of copyrighted works without the copyright owner’s permission, depending on the facts and statutory requirements.

Fourth Idly may consider applicable legal exceptions when reviewing a copyright complaint. Users should not assume that every use is infringing merely because the copyright owner did not provide a separate written licence; similarly, Users should not assume that a use is lawful merely because the content is available online.
